title: Dawn of the Arcana
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Princess Nakaba of Senan, scorned for her red hair, is married to Prince Caesar of rival Belquat as a near-hostage, with only her half-Ajin attendant Loki at her side. She discovers her Arcana of Time, a feared power to see past and future. Caught in a love triangle and in war between the kingdoms, she works to change the injustice suffered by the Ajin, a half-animal people forced into labor.
life_message: A ruler's duty is to see the truth and work for justice and equality, even at the cost of personal happiness.

content.note: War between kingdoms; Nakaba's mother butchered; a prince killed (Wikipedia; AniList War, Tragedy).
Tragedy and slaughter of Arcana bearers (Wikipedia; MangaUpdates Tragic Past).
Arranged political marriage, possessive prince ('You are my property', publisher blurb), love triangle; a child by the end (Wikipedia).
Loneliness and childhood bullying (Wikipedia; MangaUpdates Loneliness).
Possessive romance at the start (publisher blurb; MangaUpdates Possessive Lover/s).

dominant: Discrimination and equality; duty of royalty; romance in political marriage

frames.concerns: Seeing the future through hereditary power; war.

frames.aligns: Marriage honored and faithful in the end.
frames.concerns: Visions of the future through innate power.

frames.aligns: Vocation of a princess to serve her people.
Fantasy with a clear moral vision.

Equal dignity for Ajin and humans.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Royal honor and revenge drive killings (Loki kills Cain) (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Rebellion for Ajin freedom versus royal order.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Story argues against class and race hierarchy (MangaUpdates Social Hierarchy, Discrimination).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Hereditary Arcana and monarchy with reformist goals.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: War survival balanced with Nakaba's own choices.

folkways.japan: A Western-styled fantasy court in shoujo form; the red-hair stigma echoes Japanese sensitivity to standing out.

delivery.evidence: Reviewers note politics and discrimination themes within romance and adventure (Wikipedia reception) (to verify).

delivery.note: Equality is carried by Nakaba's and Loki's choices; defenders of hierarchy are mostly obstacles (to verify).

winners_losers: Nakaba and Caesar move both kingdoms toward reform; Loki dies for the cause; discrimination loses sympathy.
